scenario_028|free_school_meals_eligible: PolicyEngine determined that this Pennsylvania household of four receives free school meal support in 2026, so the value is 1. School meals count the household's income of $61,277: $60,000 of wages, $10 of interest and $1,267 of child support received. That is 1.86 times the $33,000 poverty guideline for a household of four, above the 185% limit for reduced-price meals, so on income alone both meals are in the paid tier. Pennsylvania provides a free breakfast to students at participating schools regardless of household income, reimbursed to the extent funds are available (Act 33 of 2023, 24 P.S. § 13-1337.1(c.2)), and PolicyEngine assumes the children attend such a school, so breakfast is in the free tier for the household's three K-12 children while lunch stays paid. PolicyEngine values that breakfast at $1,112.40 for the year: $2.06 a school day for each child (the $2.90 daily subsidy less the $0.84 paid-meal rate) over 180 school days. That free school meal support is positive, so the value is 1.
scenario_031|snap: PolicyEngine calculated a SNAP benefit of $288 for this California household in 2026: the $24 monthly minimum allotment for each of the twelve months. The household is one 67-year-old, so the elderly-or-disabled rules apply. Its countable gross income is $1,987.79 a month ($9,445.47 of Social Security, $13,608.00 of private pension income and $800.00 of IRA distributions a year), within the limit of California's Modified Categorical Eligibility, 200% of the monthly poverty guideline for one person ($2,608.33 on the $1,304.17 guideline through September, $2,660 on the $1,330 guideline from October), and its $4,200 of bank assets pass the asset test. That makes the household categorically eligible for CalFresh, which waives the net income test, so its net income of $1,611 a month, above the guideline in every month, does not disqualify it. The benefit formula gives the $298 maximum allotment less 30% of net income ($484), which is below zero, so as an eligible one-person household it receives the $24 minimum allotment (7 U.S.C. 2017(a)) each month: $288 for the year.
